summaryPoints: Australia recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by Steve Smith's resolute 144 to post 284.
England replied strongly with 374, powered by Rory Burns's commanding century (133) to swing the contest.
A ruthless second-innings declaration at 487/7d by Australia established a massive 398 Runs target.
Nathan Lyon spearheaded Australia's attack to bowl out England for 146 and seal victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Edgbaston commenced with high tactical intensity as Australia posted 284/10 (80.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, England countered with 374/10 (135.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Nathan Lyon (6/49), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Steve Smith delivered a masterclass for Australia (286 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Australia 65%) and allowing Australia to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, England faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Australia's bowling unit, bolstered by Nathan Lyon (12 Runs & 9 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Australia won by 251 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Australia's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While England produced fighting phases, Australia won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
